a.title: hermes-sync peer-partial: classify missing install-stamp and transient codesign -dv failures correctly (PR #2058 review nits)
a.body:
Follow-up from exact-head review 5888975887 on PR #2058 (https://github.com/softmax-universe/daveey-hermes/pull/2058#pullrequestreview-5888975887), softmax-universe/daveey-hermes, base `state`, file `hermes-sync`. PR #2058 merged as eb032c4aed.

Non-blocking nits to address:
1. A missing install-stamp.json raises FileNotFoundError, which fetch_peer_partial treats as transient, so it recopies on every pass. Decide: a complete copy with no stamp is a verify-class failure (memoize), or skip the peer cheaply before copying.
2. Stamp JSON that is not a dict raises AttributeError and escapes (pre-existing). Treat it as a verify failure.
3. The codesign calls in verify_prebuilt_app have no timeout. Add them so the 2 h .peer-partial-tmp keep window bounds verify.
4. A transient `codesign -dv` failure reads as ad-hoc and is memoized (pre-existing). Distinguish a nonzero exit or timeout (transient, do not memoize) from a real ad-hoc signature.

Add a test for each. Open one PR against `state`, get an independent exact-head review, and merge on green CI.

a.title: core: Kanban restart-continuation should keep a stopped call's own result below the interrupted stamp (sibling of PR #2062)
a.body:
Follow-up from review 5889241381 on softmax-universe/daveey-hermes PR #2062 (t_01a1d41fd158579d).

PR #2062 made `agent/update_pause_cancel.committed` keep a cancelled tool call's own result below the update stamp (`with_own_result`: head 1536 + tail 512 chars, closing `[end of the cancelled call's own result]` line). The sibling path `gateway/session_kanban_continue._answer_interrupted_calls` (restart continuation of a Kanban run) still overwrites each stopped tool row (`_stop_result_rows`) with the bare `interrupted_result(at)` text, so a killed command's own `[Command interrupted]` partial output (e.g. a Terraform apply log, a job_id) is still dropped there.

Fix: in `_answer_interrupted_calls`, for each stopped row being rewritten, read its current content and, when it is the tool's own text result (not the executor's cancel/skip text), write `with_own_result(stamp, own)` instead of the bare stamp (reuse the helper from agent/update_pause_cancel.py). Appended rows for unanswered calls keep the bare stamp. Add a test in tests/ next to test_kanban_restart_continuation. Land via `hermes-core-wt ship`.

a.title: Victim scan on worker-2: live wake_checks with redactor-masked values (t_01a1cf477dece56b f)
a.body:
Read-only victim scan for t_01a1cf477dece56b (acceptance f). Run it on **this machine** (worker-2) and report the counts.

Background: kanban park probes (`wake_check`) used to go through the display secret redactor before they were stored. A probe containing `idempotency_key='…'`, `*_token=…` or a similar name could be stored masked (`…`, `***`, `«redacted`), and then it never matches. The fix is in PR #1354. This scan finds live probes that are already damaged.

Run this exactly, read-only (`mode=ro`). Never edit `task_wake_checks` rows.
```
python3 - <<'EOF'
import glob, os, re, sqlite3, socket
pat = re.compile(r"(?i)[a-z0-9_]*(?:key|token|secret|password|passwd|credential|auth)[a-z0-9_]*\s*[=:]\s*['\"]?[^\s'\"]*?(?:\.\.\.|\*\*\*|«redacted)")
dbs = glob.glob(os.path.expanduser("~/.hermes/kanban.db")) + glob.glob(os.path.expanduser("~/.hermes/kanban/boards/*/kanban.db")) + glob.glob(os.path.expanduser("~/.hermes/profiles/*/kanban.db"))
live = victims = 0
for db in dbs:
    try:
        rows = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db}?mode=ro", uri=True).execute("select task_id, cmd from task_wake_checks").fetchall()
    except sqlite3.Error as e:
        print(db, "ERR", e); continue
    live += len(rows)
    for tid, cmd in rows:
        if cmd and pat.search(cmd):
            victims += 1; print("VICTIM", db, tid, pat.search(cmd).group(0)[:60])
print(socket.gethostname(), "dbs", len(dbs), "live_wake_checks", live, "victims", victims)
EOF
```
For each VICTIM line, comment on t_01a1cf477dece56b (or ask an operator to) with the task id and the masked fragment, and do NOT print the full command. A victim's owner must re-park with a correct probe; do not rewrite the row.

Complete with metadata `{"host": "<hostname>", "dbs": N, "live_wake_checks": N, "victims": N, "victim_task_ids": [...]}`, and put the printed final line in the summary.

If it's not installed yet, first confirm `git -C ~/.hermes/repos/hermes-state merge-base --is-ancestor f590554f8aa7663090b59dd71870c04eda6090fd HEAD` exits 0. Then run the same idempotent step the updater runs: `/usr/bin/python3 ~/.hermes/repos/hermes-state/hosts/hermes-workers/install-github-quota.py`. If the state clone doesn't have f590554f yet, wait for the next `hermes-core-update` pass (every 10 min), up to 30 min. Don't edit the checkout.
2. Confirm card shells still work: `gh pr view 1478 -R softmax-universe/daveey-hermes --json state` and, in a scratch dir, `git -c credential.helper= -c credential.helper='!~/.local/bin/gh auth git-credential' ls-remote https://github.com/softmax-universe/daveey-hermes.git refs/heads/state` must both succeed.
3. Guard proof: `token-broker exec --scope user/github --reason "guard proof t_01a1cedd5cab762d" -- gh api rate_limit --jq .resources.core`
4. `sqlite3 -header ~/.hermes/logs/github-quota/audit.sqlite "select id,fingerprint,reason,executable,exit_code,host,started from vends where reason='guard proof t_01a1cedd5cab762d'"`. a.title: Backfill pre-fix attachment bytes from worker-3 to Board blob store (52 hub rows)
a.body:
## Goal
Copy the bytes of hub attachment rows that were completed on **hermes-worker-3** before its core had the worker-attachment-custody fix (daveey/hermes c2b5952cca, PR1161) up to the Board blob store, under their ORIGINAL uid, so the hub can read them through the normal attachment path. Follow-up from t_01a1ca91167d8889 (backfill acceptance item 3).

## Why these rows don't self-heal
Worker kanban mirrors drop finished cards. A row whose card finished before the fix was installed never got a blob_key, and its local row is now gone, so `transfer_pending` can't upload it. The files usually still exist under `~/.hermes/kanban/attachments/<task>/[<uid>/]<filename>`. On worker-2 this recovered 12 of 12 rows (all hub-verified).

## Snapshot (hub, 2026-11-12 ~07:40Z)
52 rows on this host (claim lock `hermes-worker-3:*`): hub `/home/ubuntu/.hermes/kanban/evidence/t_01a1ca91167d8889/gaps-hermes-worker-3.json`, sha256 `0b8bce024bda039e331de156c9e97941d8e9b61dd34c2b45d193b1fc94c332c1`.

## Steps
1. Confirm that this host's installed core contains the fix: `git -C ~/.hermes/hermes-agent merge-base --is-ancestor c2b5952cca73cbc5b9f4ce4030566089796a09ca HEAD`. If it doesn't, `kanban_schedule` with that command as `wake_check` (awaiting kind=deploy, hermes-core-update). Uploads need the installed `Hub.put_attachment`. Hub evidence says worker-3 started uploading blobs at ~07:21Z, so it's probably installed already.
2. After install, take a fresh gap list, since rows can be added until install: `hub-admin "sqlite3 -json ~/.hermes/kanban.db \"select a.uid,a.task_id,a.filename,a.size,a.created_at,(select coalesce(json_extract(e.payload,'\$.lock'),'') from task_events e where e.task_id=a.task_id and e.kind='claimed' and e.created_at<=a.created_at+5 order by e.id desc limit 1) as claim from task_attachments a where coalesce(a.stored_path,'')='' and coalesce(a.blob_key,'')=''\"" > hub-gaps.json`. Keep only `claim` starting with `hermes-worker-3:` (jq). If `hub-admin` is missing here, use the snapshot file above, fetched through any hub read you have.
3. `scp -O hub-admin:/home/ubuntu/.hermes/kanban/evidence/t_01a1ca91167d8889/worker_gap_backfill.py .` and check its sha256 is `83fd9e5d66c22bc9d6399523f12b6edcb167f6c7545db61a9ba2e52b452ebf0e`. Run `python3 worker_gap_backfill.py hub-gaps.json results.json --dry-run`, then run it again without `--dry-run`. The script only matches by task/filename/exact size, uploads under the hub uid, then GETs the blob and compares bytes. It never writes a DB. A `hub 429` means rate-limited: wait about 60 s and rerun only the failed rows.
4. Hub-side check: `scp -O results.json hub-admin:/home/ubuntu/.hermes/kanban/evidence/t_01a1ca91167d8889/results-hermes-worker-3.json`, then `hub-admin "cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent && HERMES_HOME=/home/ubuntu/.hermes .venv/bin/python /home/ubuntu/.hermes/kanban/evidence/t_01a1ca91167d8889/hub_verify_uids.py /home/ubuntu/.hermes/kanban/evidence/t_01a1ca91167d8889/results-hermes-worker-3.json"`. Every uploaded row must print `normal_read_verified`.
5. Complete. Report the count of uploaded+hub-verified rows and name every `no_local_source` or `size_mismatch` row (uid, task, filename) as unavailable on this host. Attach results.json and the verify output.

Out of scope: the 31 historical worker-1 rows (old host 100.97.140.7 is offline). Don't touch the DB directly, and don't create new attachment rows.

a.title: Terraform 1a W3: Energy filter 1/3, write tools/balance.nim (plan Task 16b)
a.body:
Terraform milestone 1a, Wave 3 (gods without a model, plan Phase 3), Task 16b part 1 of 3: write the energy-filter tool. Orchestration spec: `docs/HANDOFF.md` in softmax-universe/coworld-terraform (hub checkout `~/code/coworld-terraform`). Read the Phase 3 introduction of the plan and design 4.9 before starting. The task text below is copied from the plan at commit 95253d6. Task 18 (`gods.nim`) and everything under it are on main.

Your part is Step 1 and the first half of Step 4 (commit `tools/balance.nim`). Do NOT run Step 2 on hermes-hub and do not write `docs/spikes/energy-balance.md`: the next two cards do those. The checks, the gods, the floor of the careful culler and the seeds are fixed in this text.

Decided here so the run card needs no judgement: `build/balance` takes `--source=allowance|life|sacrifice` (default: all three) and `--seeds=A..B` (default `1000..1019`); it prints the CSV header and rows to stdout and the pass/fail lines after them, each starting with `CHECK`, as `CHECK <source> <1-5> PASS|FAIL <the numbers behind it>`; the exit code is 0 whatever the checks say (a failing source is a finding, not an error).

## What to build

### Task 16b: The scripted energy filter

Design 4.9: before any model plays, check with scripted gods whether an energy source can be broken. This is a
filter. The default is chosen in Phase 8 with a model playing; until then it is the allowance.

**Files:**
- Create: `tools/balance.nim`
- Create: `docs/spikes/energy-balance.md`

**Step 1: Write the tool**

`tools/balance.nim` imports `terraform/[world, energy, actions, metrics, objectives, episode, gods]`. Its exploit
gods are the two cullers from `gods.nim` (`cullGod()`, which culls to the last fox, and `cullGod(floor = 3)`,
which stops at three) and these, each a `God` like those in `gods.nim`:

```nim
proc spammer(): God =
  ## As many of the cheapest action as it can pay for, every turn.
  result = proc(run: var Run) =
    for n in 0 ..< 400:
      if not run.act(Action(kind: Rain, cell: int16(n mod Cells), amount: 1, text: "spam")).accepted: break

proc hoarder(): God =
  ## Saves to the cap, then spends it all on rabbits on its last turn.
  result = proc(run: var Run) =
    if run.world.epoch == GodEpochs - 1:
      for cell in 0 ..< Cells:
        discard run.act(Action(kind: Spawn, species: Rabbit, cell: int16(cell), amount: 5, text: "dump"))

proc lateStarter(inner: God): God =
  ## Does harm for 20 epochs, then plays the heuristic: can a bad start be recovered?
  let harm = badGod()
  result = proc(run: var Run) =
    if run.world.epoch < 20: harm(run) else: inner(run)
```

For each `EnergySource`, each `Objective` and seeds 1000-1019 it plays: heuristic, do-nothing, bad, spammer,
the all-out culler, the careful culler, hoarder, and the late-starting heuristic (`newRun(seed, objective, source)`), and prints one CSV row per
source and objective with the mean score of each god, the heuristic's energy spent by action kind, and the
correlation between energy spent and score across gods. Then, per source, the five checks of design 4.9:

1. no exploit god (spammer, either culler, hoarder) has a higher mean score than the heuristic
2. heuristic > do-nothing > bad
3. the late-starting heuristic scores at least 70% of the heuristic
4. no one action kind takes more than 80% of the heuristic's spend
5. the god that spends most is not the god that scores most, or two gods within 10% of each other's spend differ
   by more than 20% in score

The careful culler is the exploit design 4.9 prices against: "maximize rabbits by killing every fox", stopped
just short of the extinction that scores zero. The all-out culler alone would hide it. In the plan review's probe
(seeds 1000-1009, Allowance, `maximize_rabbits`) the all-out culler lost on mean score (2120 against the
heuristic's 3040, do-nothing 2365) only because 4 of its 10 runs ended in extinction. On the 6 seeds where a fox
survived it beat the heuristic on every one (mean 3533 against 3022). So expect the Allowance to fail check 1
against the careful culler at the current prices. That is a finding for `energy-balance.md` and for the choice
of source and prices in Phase 8. It is not a reason to change the check, the floor or the culler.

**Step 2: Run it (Haiku, pool worker)**

Run: `nim c -d:release -o:build/balance tools/balance.nim && build/balance > tmp/balance.csv`
Expected: 6 CSV rows and a pass/fail line per source and check. About 960 runs, 30 minutes on one core; split
`--source` across cores if it has that flag.

**Step 3: Write `docs/spikes/energy-balance.md`** (Fable reads the CSV)

The table, which sources pass all five, and for a failing source which god broke it and how. A source that fails
is not removed: it is reported, and Phase 8 runs only the sources that pass. If no source passes check 1, say
so plainly with the numbers and stop there: block the Fable card with a `human_request` (the options are a higher
kill price, a score that counts foxes, or accepting the exploit for 1a). Do not change a price in this task.

**Step 4: Commit**

```bash
git add tools/balance.nim docs/spikes/energy-balance.md
git commit -m "Scripted energy filter: three sources against exploit gods"
```

## Done when

Design 4.9: before any model plays, check with scripted gods whether an energy source can be broken. This is a
filter. The default is chosen in Phase 8 with a model playing; until then it is the allowance.

For each `EnergySource`, each `Objective` and seeds 1000-1019 it plays: heuristic, do-nothing, bad, spammer,

a.title: turn_session_activity: TUI update-pause reader should use configured desktop.auto_continue (enabled/freshness/max_attempts), not hard-coded defaults
a.body:
Follow-up to PR https://github.com/softmax-universe/daveey-hermes/pull/2545 (review nit 1, review 5896585581).

a.title: hermes-mods plugins/coach: 20 collection errors without core in plugin-suites CI (hermes_state/hermes_constants imports); make core-backed tests skip
a.body:
**Red suite found by the new plugin-suites CI (t_01a19ffd473a225f).** `.github/workflows/plugin-suites.yml` in daveey/hermes-mods runs every test-all suite on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest, Python 3.11 + 3.14, with NO Hermes core checkout (core is private; the hub-side gate covers core). `plugins/coach` is red on main there, identically on both Pythons: workflow_dispatch run https://github.com/daveey/hermes-mods/actions/runs/41719353012 (main be00681d): **0 passed, 0 failed, 20 errors, 4 skipped** (collection interrupted).

Failure output (3.14):
```
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hermes_state'
ImportError while importing test module '.../plugins/coach/tests/test_state_paths.py'.
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hermes_constants'
ERROR plugins/coach/tests/test_goal_electron_acceptance.py
ERROR plugins/coach/tests/test_goal_native_remediation.py
ERROR plugins/coach/tests/test_goal_process_adapter.py
ERROR plugins/coach/tests/test_goal_process_gateway.py ... (20 modules)
```
Cause: test modules import core (`hermes_state`, `hermes_constants`) at module level, so without core the whole suite fails to collect and none of the core-free coach tests run.

Do not delete or weaken tests; with core the suite must run the same number of tests as before.
